title: InPlaceMigrator.rescueERC20 vs top-up budget coupling can brick par-restoration mid-migration
description: rescueERC20 (src/InPlaceMigrator.sol:337-339) and the _reinjectWithTopup surplus budget (:280-281) draw from the SAME unescrowed balanceOf - totalParked quantity. An owner who pre-funds surplus for an in-progress migration, then sweeps 'stray' balance via rescueERC20 as routine housekeeping, unknowingly removes the in-flight top-up budget and triggers the L-01 surplus-underfunding revert on the next migrateIn slice. The coupling is non-obvious: the contract NatSpec advertises the principal floor (totalParked) as untouchable, so a sweep fenced ABOVE that floor reads as safe, yet it can brick an in-progress migration. Pattern-parallel to ledger 0790a76a (StableStaker.rescueERC20 sweeps the underwater buffer) but a DIFFERENT contract, different reserve (top-up surplus vs underwater buffer), distinct fingerprint.
impact: None to principal. The principal floor (totalParked) is intact and advertised as untouchable; only an in-progress migration stalls. claimTimedOut backstops user recovery. Law-3 non-obvious inter-function coupling that a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised by. Not a malicious-owner vector (suppressed under owner-trust); the kept value is the surprising coupling.
attackPath: Owner pre-funds surplus for an in-progress migration.
Owner sweeps 'stray' balance via rescueERC20 (:337-339) as routine housekeeping.
rescueERC20 and the _reinjectWithTopup surplus budget (:280-281) draw from the SAME unescrowed balanceOf - totalParked quantity.
The sweep silently removes the in-flight top-up budget -> the next migrateIn slice triggers the L-01 revert.
Recovery: re-fund surplus and re-run, or users self-exit via claimTimedOut.
recommendation: Escrow the in-flight top-up surplus (track it separately from sweepable balance) or gate rescueERC20 while a migration is open, so a housekeeping sweep cannot remove the pre-funded top-up budget.
